PRIOR ART: scripts/eval/routing-eval/rules/translation-lift-v1.json — non-inferiority of the English made from two OCR reads (an OCR-engine question, margin 0.25, min 6 pairs); scripts/eval/routing-eval/rules/margin-v1.json — failure counts and by-eye wins with no reference. Neither states the routing card's three-part effect test for a COSTLIER translation model per language with a registered pool. This file is that test as data; the functions are cardVerdict / effectBeyondFloor / heterogeneity in scripts/eval/lib/routing-rules.mjs.
registered: 2026-10-06, before the book draw, before any arm ran and before any page was judged (#5873 option b). The first-run pages (T4, T5) were already scored and all point the same way; that is why guard G1 exists.
question: Per language: does Flash instead of Lite for translation (#5740, live) keep its place under the routing card once the language has 30 referenced books?
metric: fidelity (1-5), mean of two blind Opus judges per page; effect = Flash minus Lite, paired by page
a_vs_a: lite2 minus lite, same pages, same run
floor: per pool: the A-vs-A interval over the pool's combined pages (first run + top-up)

HAP.first_run: xlref-t4-2026-10 (52 books; lite = prod-A, lite2 = prod-B, flash = flash-0, packet 1)

pooling: first run + top-up pooled per language and per pool; registered here, before the second draw. A pool is used only if heterogeneity() passes (every language with >= 10 books has the pool's sign and the pooled effect lies inside its 95% interval) and the pool reaches 50 books and passes the effect test.
language_is: the language of the PAGE (eval-design 3.2), as the alignment agent records it; Aramaic pages found in Hebrew-labelled books count as Aramaic and are reported, not decided (n < 30)

stake_usd.source: results/ref-topup-5873-2026-10/census.json (2026-10-06): untranslated pages x $0.00094 (T5 Batch: Flash $0.00178 - Lite $0.00084)

small_corpus: Pali has 26 live books. If every live Pali book has been tried, its cell is a census k of 26, is treated as directional, and decides a small or medium tier only (card, small-corpus rule).

verdicts.keeps: n >= 30 (or the census), and the language's line on the card clears: its own Flash-Lite effect has a 95% interval excluding 0, a point estimate outside the pool's A-vs-A interval and >= 0.25; or the pool is usable and the language's own point estimate is >= 0.25. And guard G1 holds.
verdicts.reverses: n >= 30 (or the census), and either the upper 95% bound of Flash-Lite is under 0.25 (the data exclude the minimum effect) or the point estimate is <= 0. The proposal is then to return that language's translation to Lite; it goes to Derek as a DECISION line and is never applied here.
verdicts.still_insufficient: anything else: n short of 30 with no census, or an effect neither shown nor excluded, or G1 fails. The verdict names what is missing.

guards.G1_fresh_pages: a language with >= 10 top-up pages whose top-up-only point estimate is <= 0 cannot be 'keeps', whatever the combined set says (the first run's sign was known when this rule was written)
guards.gate: wrong-page, planted-change and duplicate controls pass for both judges (score.mjs --gate-only), or no verdict is issued
guards.exclusions: a page enters a language's effect when lite and flash both returned text and both judges scored both; a page whose reference cut both judges call 'wrong' is dropped and listed. Nothing else is dropped.

tier_note: A 'keeps' verdict says the per-language line is met. What the tier still owes is reported beside it and not waived: medium needs the registered pool at decision grade (or a replication); large (Chinese) needs decision grade, a replication on >= 30 fresh books and a judge calibrated against readers, none of which this top-up can supply.
replication_of_pool: The HAP top-up is 43 fresh books. If its own pooled effect passes the effect test alone, it is reported as a replication of the T4 pool. The SPC top-up (17 books) cannot be one.
secondary_not_in_rule: served fidelity with CI per language (an absolute judged number: reported, decides nothing without human calibration)
